interviewQuestions.question: Why is logistic regression still used in production at scale?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
I'd point to speed and auditability, not just accuracy. Inference is a dot product plus a sigmoid — microseconds per request, single core. Training stays stable at millions of rows.

The bigger reason: each coefficient exponentiates to an odds ratio, so a risk team can point to exactly why a loan was denied — a hard requirement in credit and insurance. A boosted model might add a couple AUC points but loses that auditability and costs more to serve.

It stays the default model — often the production one — whenever the accuracy gain isn't worth the latency and explainability trade-off.

**Testing:** justifying a "boring" model choice on production constraints, not leaderboard accuracy.
interviewQuestions.subTitle: Why logistic regression survives in production
